subject: problems with shiny installation in debian

messages.author: fc439899b88457c2
messages.subject: problems with shiny installation in debian
parts:
Hi,

I tried to install shiny-server on Debian. Everything went smoothly, i.e. had no glitches in compiling from the source and following the instructions here:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/Building-Shiny-Server-from-Source

When launching shiny-server after installation however, I got the following message (I'm retyping from screenshot, so ignore the typos):

module.js:356
  Module._extensions[extension](this, filename);
                                                   ^
Error: Module version mismatch. Expected 11, got 1.
   at Module.load (module.js:356:32)
   at Function.Module._load (module.js:312:12)
   at Module.require (module.js:364:17)
   at require (module.js:380:17)
   at Object.<anonymous> (/usr/local/shiny-server/lib/core/fsutil.js:16:13)
   at Module._compile (module.js:456:26)
   at Object.Module._extensions..js (module.js:474:10)
   at Module.load (module.js:356:32)
   at Function.Module._load (module.js:312:12)
   at Module.require (module.js:364:17)


I searched on google and found the following suggestion at stackverflow:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/20099334/error-module-version-mismatch-expected-11-got-1

I.e. I need to update the npm packages. I suppose this involves shiny-server package. But shouldn't this be covered by installation process? The problem is that there was an older version of shiny-server installed, which I removed. I suspect that maybe there is some conflict there. What can I start to look for problems? Reinstall npm?

I would be grateful for any pointers, I do not expect full solution.

Vaidotas Zemlys

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: problems with shiny installation in debian
parts:
Hi Vaidotas,

All the modules Shiny Server depends on should have indeed been bundled up in the installer as you expected. So you shouldn't need to provide any npm libraries on your server in order for this to work.

In fact, I suspect that an old npm module is being found and trying to be used when we should be using the one provided in the installer. 

When you uninstalled the old shiny-server package, how did you do it? We have a guide for upgrading from an old npm version (0.3.x): 

http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#upgrading-from-shiny-server-0.3.x

Can you try that commands we provide there?

Thanks,
Jeff
